heading: Sadio Mané is building a $20 million mango empire in his village, after already building a school, hospital, mosque and petrol station
author: Edited by: Soror Shaiza / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /  Sep 21, 2026, 21:00 IST
paragraphs: Sadio Mané has spent much of his career putting money back into Bambali, the Senegalese village where he was born, funding a mosque, school, hospital, petrol station and bakery along the way

At 34, the footballer is putting 11.7 billion CFA francs, about $20 million, of his own money into an agro-industrial project designed to turn Bambali's mango harvest into a business.Mané is putting $20 million into Bambali's mango industryMané laid the foundation stone for SM10 Agro in Bambali on September 19, beginning construction on a 500-hectare agro-industrial park that he says he is financing entirely himself.According to Business Insider Africa, the project represents an investment of 11.7 billion CFA francs, or about $20.4 million, making it one of Mané's largest investments outside football

Construction is expected to take 18 months and the project will include four processing units, an agricultural training centre and a research operation alongside the orchards.The scale is substantial, with plans to plant approximately 78,000 mango trees and create more than 1,000 direct jobs once operations begin.SM10 Agro is expected to process up to 8,500 tonnes of mangoes a year, while the first harvest from the new plantation is projected in about three years.Mangoes are at the centre of the project because Bambali, in Senegal's Moyenne-Casamance region, produces large quantities of the fruit but loses a significant portion of the crop because there is limited storage and processing capacity and not enough buyers for the harvest.Mané's project will sort and export fresh mangoes while also processing the fruit into mango purée, dried mango and mango butter, with guava also included in the production plans.The products are intended for sale in Senegal as well as export markets across Africa, Europe and the Middle East.“I want the fruits of the land to stay here,” Mané said.From giving money away to building something that producesThe mango project adds another layer to the work Mané has already carried out in Bambali, but the objective is different from his earlier community spending.Over the past decade, Mané has funded a mosque, school, hospital and petrol station in his hometown, while also providing free internet access and regularly supporting families in the village.He opened a bakery last November, continuing a pattern of investing directly in services and infrastructure that residents can use.SM10 Agro is intended to move beyond that model by creating a production business around resources already available in the region.The project is designed to address the problem of a highly perishable crop by processing mangoes into products that can be stored for longer and sold in more markets, rather than relying almost entirely on fresh-fruit sales.The promoters of SM10 Agro project that the operation could become profitable in its second year, with projected returns of more than 100 per cent on the investment.Alongside the commercial operation, the agricultural college and research component are intended to provide training and support around the wider agricultural activity.The investment therefore combines farming, processing, research, training and export under the same project, rather than limiting the business to growing and selling mangoes.Mané is building a business beyond footballThe project comes as Mané continues to build a life beyond the football career that made him one of Senegal's most recognisable sporting figures.He is 34 and retired from international football after Senegal's dramatic 3–2 extra-time defeat to Belgium in the Round of 32 at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, finishing as his country's all-time leading scorer with 54 goals and also holding the national record for assists with 29Mané finished second in the 2022 Ballon d'Or voting and won the Socrates Prize that year for his work away from football.At club level, he played for Liverpool and Bayern Munich before moving to Saudi Arabia, where he continues his playing career.His agricultural investment now places him among a group of prominent investors involved in Senegal's farming and food-production sector.Senegalese coverage has included Mané alongside Sedima, the poultry and agribusiness group founded by Babacar Ngom, Industries Chimiques du Sénégal, the sovereign investment fund Fonsis, and the rice company Ciriz.The combination covers very different types of investors, from a footballer using his personal fortune to established private companies, an industrial group and a state-backed fund, but they are all putting capital into agriculture and food production.For Mané, SM10 Agro also gives his hometown a new kind of investment to add to the school, hospital, mosque, petrol station and bakery he has already helped
